thread:
maria: Quick heads-up — ran a full perf sweep on mixtral-8x with AWQ int8 (latest runtime kernels). Seeing a consistent ~18% p99 tail for batches >= 6 when kv-prefetch is ON. attaching short traces below.

ajay: ugh. do we know if this is kernel selection or batching heuristic?

maria: initial signal points to kernel selector picking the AVX-int8 path for big batches; fallback to fp16 avoids the spike.

claire: can you paste the perf numbers?

maria: sure — short dump: ```
model: mixtral-8x
quant: awq-int8
batch: 8
prefetch: enabled
mean latency: 82ms
p95: 130ms
p99: 490ms
fallback (fp16 path): p99: 210ms
CPU kernel-switch overhead: +40ms
kv-hit-rate: 0.86
kv-evict-ratio: 0.12
```

sergey: interesting that kv-hit-rate is still high. suggests prefetch work + large microbatch interaction. maybe the continuous-batcher is coalescing too aggressively and kernel selector mispredicts seq-len distribution.

ajay: I saw similar with qwen-14b int8 earlier, but there we had rope-scale mismatch triggering extra kv copies. did you check RoPE config?

maria: yes — mixtral kernel expects rope_scale=1.02 for this checkpoint; runtime was using 1.0 after a recent model pin migration. small mismatch causes extra head reshuffle in the kernel path, which explodes cache-touch patterns.

claire: so two hypotheses: (1) prefetch + big microbatch -> selector chooses int8 path that does a headwise transpose leading to cache-line churn, (2) rope_scale mismatch forces corrective ops in-kernel. both plausible.

ajay: can we reproduce with a minimal local run? try: ```bash
./tools/profile --model mixtral-8x --quant awq-int8 --batch 8 --prefetch on --rope-scale 1.02 --trace-kernel selector,kv
```

maria: started that locally, attaching smaller trace — pattern: when kernel_selector.fallback_threshold is 0.12 it prefers awq-int8; raising threshold to 0.2 forces an fp16 fallback earlier and eliminates the p99 cliff.

sergey: config snippet that reproduced: ```
kernel_selector_prefer: "awq-int8"
kernel_selector_fallback_threshold: "0.20"
batcher_max_microbatch: "4"
kv_prefetch: "on"
```

claire: but we can't just bump fallback_threshold globally — that hurts throughput and cost on normal workloads. need a smarter policy: prefer-int8 only when hot-kv-hit-rate > 0.9 AND avg-seq <= 512.

ajay: agreed. propose adding a fast profiler metric that the selector reads at route-time: estimated_kv_touch_ratio and seq_len_histogram.

maria: also ran a quant-accuracy check: for mixtral-8x on our instruction eval set: AWQ-int8 delta = -0.7% top-1, GPTQ-int8 delta = -0.3%, FP8 ~ -0.1%. AWQ gives better perf but higher accuracy delta here.

sergey: curious numbers. can we include calibration prompts used? sometimes AWQ calibration prompts matter a lot.

maria: used the standard 512-token diverse set + long-context anchors (5 samples with 2k tokens each). sample prompts: "Summarize the following technical document..." and a long legal contract paragraph.

claire: we should try AWQ with micro-calib: 50-shot mix of short (<=128) + mid (512) prompts; awq sometimes overfits long anchors and hurts mainstream prompts.

ajay: action items: (1) bisect kernel versions 2.3.1 -> 2.3.4 to see when head-reshuffle changed, (2) run route-time selector proto that reads kv_hit_rate and seq_hist, (3) run AWQ micro-calib and GPTQ baseline on same anchor set and compare.

maria: starting bisect now. initial note: 2.3.3 introduced a vectorized head-reshape that assumes rope_scale pinned; that's likely culprit.

sergey: for the selector proto, here's a tiny heuristics patch I sketched: ```
if (estimated_kv_touch_ratio > 0.9 && avg_seq <= 512 && kv_prefetch_on) {
  prefer_awq = true;
} else if (avg_seq > 1024 || kv_eviction_ratio > 0.1) {
  prefer_fp16 = true;
}
```

claire: please add unit tests simulating hotset tail latencies. even a synthetic workload with alternating long/short seqs reproduces selector flip.

ajay: on the quant side, record: AWQ-int8 gave best speed but worst accuracy here; GPTQ-int8 is middle ground; FP8 keeps accuracy but needs kernel changes for stability (we saw seed-dependent variability).

maria: final note — we'll need a rollout plan: 1) patch selector to consult fast stats, 2) disable the vectorized head-reshape on 2.3.3+ for awq-int8 until we enforce rope_scale checks, 3) run AWQ micro-calib experiments across mixtral/mistral/qwen/llama on dev cluster, capturing eval deltas and tail-latency p99.

claire: assigning: maria -> bisect + short traces, ajay -> selector prototype, sergey -> micro-calib sweep infra. I'll own rollout gating.
